HCI1.title: Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)
HCI1.content:
Overview of HCI

Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) refers to the study and design of the interaction between people (users) and computers. It focuses on creating user-friendly interfaces and experiences.

Multidisciplinary Field

HCI draws on multiple disciplines to build efficient systems:

  • Engineering: Creating efficient systems and interfaces.
  • Psychology: Understanding user behavior and cognition.
  • Design: Making systems attractive and usable.
  • Ergonomics: Fitting the system to the human body and needs.

HCI2.title: Guidelines Categories and General HCI Design
HCI2.content:
Types of Guidelines

HCI guidelines are typically specific, task-based, user-group focused, or platform-dependent. Categories include:

  • User Type: Kids, elderly, people with disabilities.
  • Platform/System: Mobile, desktop, embedded systems, public kiosks.
  • Vendor/Brand: iOS, Android, Windows, company branding.
  • Interaction Style: GUI, voice input, gesture, touchscreen, haptics.
  • Task Context: Driving, shopping, outdoor use, eyes-free scenarios.
  • Application Type: Games, e-commerce, social media, navigation.

General Design Guidelines

General rules cover visual display layout, information structuring, taking user input, and designing for users with disabilities (such as providing keyboard-only navigation for users who do not use a mouse or touchscreen).
